intro: This guide explains what each part of the app does and how to use it, in plain words.
The app is made of small apps, each doing one job. Open any of them from the main menu.
Below, each app has a short summary, a few notes on what a member can do, and simple steps where they help.

sections.title: Directory
sections.summary: A list of people and the skills they hold — members and community-nominated profiles alike.
body: Directory lists people and the skills they hold. Some profiles are made by members themselves. Others are community-generated: a member nominated someone who does not have an account yet, so the profile carries a "Community generated" badge. Signed in, you see every active, listed profile.

Open a profile to read the person's name, job title, sector, and skills. They are fellow community members sharing their skills, not a formal service. If a community-generated profile is yours, you can claim it as your own.
Directory only shows people. It does not message, book, or transact — those actions live in other apps.
howTo: Open Directory while signed in. The list of profiles loads.
Search by name or skill, or filter by sector, to find someone.
Open a profile to read their name, job title, sector, and skills.
Create your own profile, or claim a community-generated one that is yours, so others can find you.

sections.title: Foundation
sections.summary: Find a support provider and connect with them one to one.
body: Foundation lets you search providers by name, headline, or bio, and filter by the skill they offer. Providers are fellow community members who chose to offer help — not a formal service.

When you want help, request a quote or connect. That opens a private one-to-one chat between you and the provider. Voice and video calls are available once connected, and a call may cost ServiceCredits, shown in credits only.
Private chat exists only inside an active connection or quote — there is no open inbox to message anyone. When the connection ends, the chat closes.
howTo: Open Foundation. The provider list loads with each provider's name, headline, and bio.
Search by name or words from a provider's headline or bio, or filter by an offered skill, to find a provider that fits.
Request a quote or connect to open a private chat with them.
Start a voice or video call once connected.

sections.title: Chyme
sections.summary: One shared audio room where members can talk and chat.
body: Chyme is a single shared audio room. Join the call to talk with other members, or type in the chat panel.
You start muted and can mute or unmute your own microphone. You can send a Tip in ServiceCredits to another participant from their tile.
Signed-out visitors get a free listen view and must sign in to speak.
howTo: Open Chyme signed in. The room, participant list, and chat panel load.
Press join to enter the audio room. You start muted; mute and unmute yourself as you like.
Type in the chat panel to send a message; it stays after reload.
Use the Tip action on another participant's tile to send them ServiceCredits.

sections.title: SocketRelay
sections.summary: Post a request for help and connect with a member who offers to fill it.
body: SocketRelay is a feed of member requests. Post a request with a title and one to three tags; others browse and filter the feed by tag.
A member can offer to help by claiming a request, which opens a private chat between the two of you to work it out.
Your own posts stay in your feed even after they expire, shown dimmed with a Re-post button. The Direct Line tab lists the conversations you are waiting on or talking through.
howTo: Open SocketRelay signed in. The feed of requests loads.
Post your own request with a title and one to three tags.
Claim a request to help; a private chat opens with the poster.
Open the Direct Line tab to see your active conversations.

sections.title: Beacon
sections.summary: Watch a live broadcast and chat during it if signed in.
body: Beacon is a one-way live broadcast anyone can watch with the link — no sign-in needed. When nothing is live, a calm "No live event right now" screen shows, with the last replay if there is one.
Signed-in members can post chat messages and send reactions during the event. Signed-out viewers see a "sign in to chat" prompt.
The broadcast is marked as live and public so everyone knows their comments are visible. After the event, the recording is watchable.
howTo: Open Beacon. If nothing is live, you see the idle screen or the last replay.
During a live event, watch the broadcast — no account needed.
Sign in to post chat messages and send reactions.

sections.title: PeerProgramming
sections.summary: A weekly small-group room built around a shared topic.
body: PeerProgramming places active members into small weekly groups of about five people. When you are assigned, you get an in-app notice with the group and the week's topic.
The room is text-first with a topic header and supports threaded replies. The timeline stays and comes back after you reconnect.
Group members can post and reply; others may have a more limited view. You can submit feedback from the room.
howTo: Open PeerProgramming. Your group loads, or you see a "not in a group yet" state.
Read the week's topic in the room header.
Post a message or reply in a thread with your group.
Submit feedback from the room when you have a suggestion.

sections.title: Mood
sections.summary: A private mood check-in you can submit once a week.
body: Mood lets you record how you are doing on a scale of 1 to 5, with an optional note. You can check in once every 7 days.
Right after submitting, the screen moves to a cooldown state until the window opens again.
The community pulse shows only an aggregate chart — no individual check-in, note, or identifier is ever shown.
howTo: Open Mood. The check-in form loads with a mood picker and an optional note.
Pick a value from 1 to 5 and submit.
Return after 7 days to check in again.

sections.title: GentlePulse
sections.summary: A library of meditations you can play, rate, and favorite.
body: GentlePulse is a library of meditations. Each card shows a title, description, tags, duration, average rating, and rating count.
Sort by newest, most-rated, or highest-rating, filter by tag, or show only your favorites.
Play a meditation to open its media. You can rate it from 1 to 5 stars and add or remove it from your favorites. A support page explains the app and its privacy statement.
howTo: Open GentlePulse. The library loads with meditations.
Play a meditation to open its media.
Give it a 1-to-5 star rating.
Add or remove it from your favorites.

sections.title: WhatWorks
sections.summary: A shared list of tools that have helped, grouped by problem.
body: WhatWorks is a shared list of everyday problems, each with tools members have found useful — an emoji, a name, a short "why it works" note, a count of how many members marked it helpful, and a direct purchase link.
Mark a tool Helpful to add your own endorsement, or toggle it off to withdraw it.

You can suggest a tool for a problem by adding a product name, a purchase link, and an optional note. Suggestions are reviewed before they appear and stay anonymous to other members. Search across tools and problems, and use the side nav to jump to a problem.
howTo: Open WhatWorks signed in. Problems load, each with its tools.
Mark a tool Helpful if it helped you; toggle off to take it back.
Suggest a tool: pick a problem, add a product name and purchase link, and submit for review.

sections.title: SkillsHunt
sections.summary: Nominate skilled people for scouting rounds and follow the leaderboard.
body: SkillsHunt runs rounds where members nominate skilled people. Browse active, upcoming, and closed rounds, and open one to see its rules, scoring, and dates.
During an active round, submit a nomination with the person's name, a short bio, their Quora profile link, and the skills they hold.
The leaderboard ranks nominations by accepted points; every number shown comes from live data. You earn achievements and in-app notices as your nominations are reviewed.
howTo: Open SkillsHunt signed in. The list of rounds loads.
Open an active round and go to the Scout tab.
Fill the "Nominate a Survivor" form — name, bio, Quora link, skills, and location — and submit.
Check the Leaderboard tab to see the ranking.

sections.title: Workforce
sections.summary: A live read-only dashboard of the community's workforce and skill gaps.
body: Workforce is a read-only tracker. The dashboard shows population, workforce total, headcount target, recruited count, recruitment progress, sector gaps, skill-level breakdown, and top training gaps, all computed live.
Drill down by sector, skill level, or occupation to see where the gaps are.
Your own Workforce profile is read-only and comes from your Directory profile; there is no editor. You can browse occupations, largest gap first.
howTo: Open the Workforce dashboard. The live numbers load.
Drill down by sector, skill level, or occupation to see the gaps.
Browse the occupations list to see demand and supply per job title.

sections.title: Skills Taxonomy
sections.summary: The shared list of sectors, job titles, and skills the rest of the app reads from.
body: Skills Taxonomy owns the shared, three-level list of sectors, job titles, and skills that other apps draw on.
As a member you can open the browser and read the sector, job title, and skill tree, but there are no create, edit, or delete controls — the list is read-only for members and maintained centrally.
The skill choices you see in other apps come from this list.
howTo: Open Skills Taxonomy signed in. The three-level tree loads.
Expand a sector to see its job titles and skills.

sections.title: ServiceCredits
sections.summary: Your wallet of ServiceCredits and where you send them to other members.
body: ServiceCredits is the app's non-money credit. Your wallet shows your available, held, and total balance, with plain labels for each kind of activity (transfer, escrow, treasury fee, adjustment).
You can send credits directly to another member. A plain send delivers immediately — the sender's balance drops and the recipient's rises with no pending step.
Credits are never shown as cash and cannot be withdrawn for real money. The Economy tab shows community totals like credits in circulation, total issued, and total burned.
howTo: Open ServiceCredits signed in. Your wallet and balance load.
Send a small amount to another member; the transfer completes right away.
Open the Economy tab to see community-wide totals.

sections.title: Contributions
sections.summary: Support the current fundraiser and log how you helped.
body: Contributions is a voluntary fundraiser. You can submit a claim of one of three kinds: a gift card (you state the amount and your Signal contact — the code is never entered in the app; you send it to the owner over Signal), a Quora comment (paste the comment link), or a GitHub star (paste your GitHub profile link).
See your own claim history and its statuses (pending, confirmed, rejected), and the cycle's collective progress toward the owner-set goals.
Contributing is optional, nothing is locked behind it, and any credits are given in recognition, not as a purchase or real money.
howTo: Open Contributions signed in. The current cycle and its progress load.
Choose one of the three cards — gift card, Quora comment, or GitHub star.
Fill the form that opens below and submit your claim.
Check your claim history for its status.

sections.title: LevelUp
sections.summary: Learning cohorts with milestones, plus a view-only credits wallet.
body: LevelUp lists learning cohorts you can filter by track, status, and start date. Open a cohort to see its curriculum, milestones, and how to enroll; enrolling may involve an optional deposit held in escrow and released per milestone.
Your dashboard shows your wallet balance, escrow totals, active enrollments, and recent transactions. You can browse trainer profiles and see achievement badges you have earned.

The Credits Wallet here is view-only — it shows credits you earned or were granted and has no spend or transfer control. If an action is not allowed for your account, the app explains why in plain words.
howTo: Open LevelUp. The cohort list loads.
Filter by track and status to narrow it.
Open a cohort to read its curriculum and milestones, then enroll.
Open the Credits Wallet to see credits you have earned (view only).

sections.title: TrustTransport
sections.summary: Request a ride, a package delivery, or food, and track it.
body: TrustTransport is one booking surface for three kinds of trips: a ride, a package, or food. Pick a mode, enter your origin and destination or location, and see quote previews before you submit.

For a ride you request, choose an offer, track the driver, and complete it. For a package you create a job with details and track its state. For food you browse providers, place an order, and confirm receipt.
Safety controls include sharing your trip status, an emergency help shortcut, and a trusted-contact visibility toggle.
howTo: Open TrustTransport signed in. The booking surface loads with the mode selector.
Choose ride, package, or food.
Enter your origin and destination and review the quote preview.
Submit the request and track it to completion.

sections.title: LightHouse
sections.summary: Browse places to stay, list your own place, and request a stay.
body: LightHouse opens straight to a browse screen of available places — no profile needed to look. Each listing shows details like title, location, and rent; rent may be in a regular currency, or a listing may accept ServiceCredits, shown with an "Accepts ServiceCredits" badge (never a cash figure for credits).

Any member can list their own place from the "List your place" tab. To request a stay on a listing you don't own, use "Request to stay"; if you have no seeker details saved yet, you are sent to the "Your details" screen first, then the request goes through.
Hosts accept or reject requests, and an accepted request opens a private chat. You can block another member for safety.
howTo: Open LightHouse. It lands on the browse screen.
Open a listing to see its details, rent, and whether it accepts ServiceCredits.
Use "Request to stay" on a listing you don't own; save your details if prompted.
To host, open "List your place" and fill in your listing.

sections.title: ClickLog
sections.summary: A private, one-tap incident counter only you can see.
body: ClickLog is a private counter for logging incidents. Press the large "Log Incident" button to record one, with an optional location or note, and your total rises by one.
You see your own total and recent history and can delete your own incidents.
The log is private to you — no one else's rows appear, and there is no public view. Sign-in is required.
howTo: Open ClickLog signed in. Your total and recent list load.
Press "Log Incident" to record one; add an optional note or location.
Delete any of your own incidents you no longer want.

sections.title: Recurring Activity
sections.summary: Record an ongoing tie with another member that both of you confirm.
body: Recurring Activity lets you declare an ongoing arrangement with another member — the other party, sector, currency, and cadence, plus a ServiceCredits value when the currency is credits. It starts as pending.
The other member confirms or declines it, and only a confirmed activity counts toward Trust or GDP. Either party can end an ongoing activity so the record stays accurate.
You control whether an activity is private (the default), restricted, or public. The hub shows your ongoing activities and any pending confirmations.
howTo: Open Recurring Activity signed in. Your ongoing activities and pending confirmations load.
Declare a new activity: pick the other member, sector, currency, and cadence.
When another member records one with you, confirm or decline it.
End an activity when it is over, or change its visibility.

sections.title: GDP
sections.summary: A live transparency report of the community's total activity value.
body: GDP is a read-only report. It shows the headline community figure — total, service, and goods/local value — with plain-language explanations, per-capita indicators, and progress toward the target goals.

You can see the breakdown by service category, provider participation and hourly-rate trends, and year-by-year rollout tracking. Freshness and definition cues show how current each figure is, and estimates are labelled.
The figure is computed live each time you load it. It is a community total, never a per-wallet money value, and no credits-to-cash line appears. Sign-in is required.
howTo: Open the GDP report signed in. The headline figure and member count load.
Read the plain-language explanations and per-capita indicators.
Open the "Value by Source" breakdown to see which apps contribute.
